findings.location: Entire article — multiple inline Scripture quotations and quoted English sentences
findings.source_quote: “Blessed are the pure in heart” (Matthew 5:8). “That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere (pure) and without offense till the day of Christ” (Philippians 1:10). “Think on things that are pure” (Philippians 4:8). “Keep thyself pure” (1Timothy 5:22). Revelation 19 says “The pure in heart shall see God.” Psalm 24:3-4 asks “Who shall see God?” The answer is “he that hath clean hands and a pure heart.” ... I John 1:6 says, “if we say that we have fellowship with Him and walk in darkness (light on the outside and darkness on the inside), we lie and do not practice the truth.” ... In John 10:10, Jesus said, “the devil wants to steal, kill, and destroy. He wants to steal your purity, kill your character, and destroy” ... Hebrews 4:13 says, “Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom (we will give account to).” ... Numbers 32:23 is still very true, saying, “Be sure your sin will find you out.” ... James 1:15 happens: “Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death” Verse 16 says, “Do not (be deceived) my beloved brethren.” ... Matthew 23:26, where He said, "Cleanse first the inside of the cup and platter that the outside may be clean also" ... James 5 says, “Confess your faults one to another that ye may be healed.” ... I Peter 5:5 tells us that God gives grace to the humble. ... Matthew 23:26, where he said: "First clean the inside of the cup, so that the outside may be clean also." ... Romans 2:16 tells of the day when God will judge the secrets of men.
findings.suggested_fix: Translate every printed English Scripture quotation into Spanish, preserving the exact sense and wording of the authoritative English text as printed in the source (i.e., render the source’s English phrasing accurately into Spanish). For example, change “Blessed are the pure in heart” (Matthew 5:8) to a Spanish rendering that directly conveys the printed English phrase (e.g., “Bienaventurados los de limpio corazón” (Mateo 5:8)), and similarly translate each in-line quotation (Matthew 23:26, James 1:15, Hebrews 4:13, etc.) so that the Spanish article contains the quoted biblical phrases in Spanish while remaining faithful to the original English text and verse numbering. Ensure parenthetical verse citations (book and chapter:verse) remain identical to the source. Do this for every occurrence where an English Bible quotation remains in the translation.
findings.translation_quote: Many Scripture quotations remain in English throughout the translation (see examples above).
